newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall on political unrest.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall on political unrest.

text.p: Israel's stock market opened with heavy supply, influenced by the political unrest between Israel and the Palestinians as well as Thursday's expiration of options on the Maof index, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares opened down 4.91 points, or 2.50 percent at 191.65. The Maof 25 index opened down 2.48 percent at 201.21.
Israeli shares fall on political unrest =2
At the start of trading there was supply of 160 million shekels against demand of only 13 million shekels, Dan Scharia of Capital Investments said.

"The market is reacting to the new Intifada (the Palestinian uprising in the late 1980s and early 1990s). It is also influenced by the expiration of options on the Maof index. If things calm down soon, so will the market. If the unrest continues there will be a negative impact on the market," he said.

Palestinian health officials said 15 Palestinians were shot dead in two days of clashes over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's opening of a tunnel beside the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, the site of Islam's third holiest shrine.

"We will have to see how trading develops today and how the political events develop. Also, we have to see the reaction of foreign investors to the events. Meanwhile there is no tendency to buy up the supply. It appers the market will fall hard today," said Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments.
